statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-9669: a bz2.BZ2Decompressor could be used again after a decompression error; an application that caught the OSError and retried with the same object could make libbz2 resume from an invalid state and, with crafted input, write past a stack buffer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/150599 (3.10 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/938ec030e90c5e53f1faac6fab1643f14e4f4a79), first released in CPython 3.10.21; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/DBJZETMGUIFK7DVUWMOXHD3Z6IX2QPSX/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-9669, which lists every 3.10 release before 3.10.21 as affected. The fix, in Modules/_bz2module.c, records the error code in a new field of the decompressor object (moving the end-of-stream flag after it) and refuses further calls with the ValueError 'Decompressor is unusable after a previous error'. Checked the compiled _bz2 extension module (lib-dynload/_bz2.cpython-310-*.so) in the python-3.10 package of every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-28, 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8, on x86_64 and aarch64 (package sizes checked against the repository index): 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.20-r9 do not contain that message and keep the end-of-stream flag at the old field offset, so they lack the fix; 3.10.20-r10 to 3.10.22-r8 contain the message and access the decompressor's fields exactly as the module built from the upstream 3.10.21 source does (error-code stores to the new field, end-of-stream flag at its new offset). In 3.10.20-r10 to 3.10.20-r13 the module is byte-identical to the one in 3.10.21-r1 on both architectures: a DHI backport made before the upstream release. The range ends at 3.10.20-r10. Builds from 3.10.20-r10 on that the CVE record still matches carry the fix.

CVE-2026-9669: a bz2.BZ2Decompressor could be reused after a decompression error, and crafted input could then make it resume from an invalid internal state and write out of bounds on a stack buffer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/150599 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/991e6cf86496718c4ef00b362d640e00cb5c85b2), first released in CPython 3.12.14: a decompressor that has failed raises ValueError('Decompressor is unusable after a previous error'). See https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/DBJZETMGUIFK7DVUWMOXHD3Z6IX2QPSX/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-9669. Checked the _bz2 extension module for the error message the fix adds (with its existing 'End of stream already reached' message as a control) in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.13-r10 lack the fix; 3.12.13-r10 and every later build have it (from that build to the last CPython 3.12.13 build it is a backport made before the 3.12.14 release; the 3.12.14 and later builds carry the upstream fix). The range ends at 3.12.13-r10.

Checked the compiled _bz2 extension module (lib-dynload/_bz2.cpython-310-*.so) in every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Debian 13 repository by 2026-11-28, 3.10.20-0 to 3.10.22-10, on amd64 and arm64 (checksums verified against the repository index); the standard library ships in libpython-3.10-stdlib up to 3.10.20-9 and in libpython-3.10-minimal from 3.10.20-10, and 3.10.20-0 to 3.10.20-2 were published as architecture-independent packages that each carry one architecture's native code (aarch64 in 3.10.20-0 and 3.10.20-1, x86_64 in 3.10.20-2): 3.10.20-0 to 3.10.20-6 do not contain that message and keep the end-of-stream flag at the old field offset, so they lack the fix; 3.10.20-7 to 3.10.22-10 contain the message, and on each architecture their machine code is the same as in 3.10.21-0, which is built from the upstream 3.10.21 source, apart from addresses: a DHI backport made before the upstream release. The range ends at 3.10.20-7. Builds from 3.10.20-7 on that the CVE record still matches carry the fix.
